e-10899.problem: Given that $y=x^3+e^x$ for $x=x(t),$ and that $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t}=2$ at the point where $x=1,$ find $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}.$
e-10899.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={x}^{3}+{e}^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{3}+{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}+{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (3{x}^{2}+{e}^{x}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t}=2$ and $x=1,$ and solve for $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (3\cdot {1}^{2}+{e}^{1}) \\ 2 & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (3+e) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{2}{3+e}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-10901.knowledge_point: Determining an Angular Rate Given a Related Rate
e-10901.problem: Given that $r=\sin\theta$ for $\theta = \theta(t),$ and that $\dfrac{\textrm d r}{\textrm d t}=\sqrt{2}$ at the point where $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4},$ find $\dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}.$
e-10901.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d r}{\textrm d t}=\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4},$ and solve for $\dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \sqrt{2} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\ \sqrt{2} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

e-10902.problem: A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y=x+e^x$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $2 \,\textrm{cm}/\textrm{s}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=5\,\textrm{cm}.$
e-10902.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =x+{e}^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x+{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x+{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (1+{e}^{x}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}=2 \,\textrm{cm}/\textrm{s}$ and $x=5$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2(1+{e}^{5})\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

content.knowledge_point: Determining an Angular Rate Given a Related Rate
content.problem: Given that $r=\theta +6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $\theta =\theta (t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}=7$ at the point where $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{6},$ find $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}.$
content.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\theta +6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\theta +6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(\theta +6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (1-6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}=7$ and $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{6},$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (1-6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =7\cdot (1-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{7\pi }{6})) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =7\cdot 4 \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =28.\end{aligned}
$$

A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+{x}^{2}$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $-4\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=3\,\,\text{cm}.$

The $y$-coordinate is changing at the rate of 
{{field-1}}
$\text{cm}/\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+{x}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+{x}^{2}] \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)+{x}^{2}] \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{1}{x+1}+2x).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=-4\,\text{cm}/\text{s}$ and $x=3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-4\cdot (\frac{1}{3+1}+2(3)) \\  & =-4\cdot (\frac{1}{4}+6) \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{25}{4} \\  & =-25.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $y$-coordinate is changing at the rate of $-25\text{ }\text{cm}/\text{s}.$

after.problem: A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y=2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x}$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $2\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=2\,\text{cm}.$
after.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (4x-3{e}^{x}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=2\,\text{cm}/\text{s}$ and $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2(4\cdot (2)-3{e}^{2})\,\text{cm}/\text{s} \\  & =2(8-3{e}^{2})\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Differentiating the given relation with respect to t using implicit differentiation, we get

y=2x2−3exddt(y)=ddt(2x2−3ex)dydt=dxdt⋅ddx(2x2−3ex)dydt=dxdt⋅(4x−3ex).

Now, we can substitute the given information dxdt=2cm/s and x=2 and get

dydt=2(4⋅(2)−3e2)cm/s=2(8−3e2)cm/s.

content.problem: A particle $P$ is moving along the curve $y=2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x}$ such that the $x$-coordinate of $P$ is changing at the rate of $2\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.$ Find the rate of change of the $y$-coordinate when $x=2\,\text{cm}.$
content.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}-3{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (4x-3{e}^{x}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=2\,\text{cm}/\text{s}$ and $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2(4\cdot (2)-3{e}^{2})\,\text{cm}/\text{s} \\  & =2(8-3{e}^{2})\,\text{cm}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$
